lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The ice is quiet, but the noise around this club has not gone away. Why hasn't Morgan Rielly been traded yet? is the question hanging over a Maple Leafs offseason that still feels unfinished, even as the club's season is long over and the focus shifts to camp, cap math and the kids pushing through the door. Toronto's top prospects are getting another hard look, and that matters because the organization can't keep living on reputation alone. Rielly, for his part, is still here - and that alone tells you the market never matched the chatter. The Maple Leafs need cleaner blue-line play and more certainty up front, not another season of wishful thinking. What happens next is simple: September brings the first real roster battle, and the prospects will have to prove they're more than promise.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: A season that already ran its course now belongs to the ledger - and the real story is what the Blue Jays do with the room they've created. Toronto's 8-3 loss to the Yankees on Sunday ended the noise and sharpened the offseason focus, with the club sitting at 64-68 in a year that asks harder questions than it answers. There's interest here, though, not drift: Jameson Taillon's forearm has become the newest health watch, and the organization has already made room on the edges with roster churn that tells you the winter is going to be active. What matters next is the work between now and spring - the pitching depth, the free-agent market, and how aggressively the Jays rebuild the spine of this club.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The offseason has a pulse again in Toronto, and it beats with one name: Kawhi Leonard. The proposed Leonard return remains unresolved while the NBA investigates the Clippers - a reminder that the Raptors' summer still hangs on league bureaucracy more than basketball. Toronto's 2025-26 season is finished, so the only number that matters now is the shape of the roster to come, not any old ledger from spring. The real intrigue is at the edges: Ja'Kobe Walter's handle and finishing remain a live question, and RJ Barrett's name keeps surfacing in trade chatter because good teams do not leave that kind of salary and scoring untouched for long. Darko Rajaković has called Scottie Barnes the center of it all. Training camp will tell whether Toronto is building around Barnes - or shuffling the deck again.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The most troubling sight in Ashburn isn't a blown assignment or a dropped ball - it's the same old center question rearing up again, right where a camp can least afford confusion. Dan Quinn said the Commanders have "got to figure out center," and that is the blunt truth after a preseason week that did nothing to calm the line's nerves. Antonio Williams, meanwhile, is forcing his way into the conversation; the rookie caught two passes for 41 yards against Detroit and looks less like a hidden project than a real option. Washington has shown enough in camp to hint at a workable roster, but not enough at the pivot. Watch the Baltimore joint practice and Friday's preseason finale - those snaps will tell you whether this line can protect a season or merely survive one.

article.title: Monday's Skate
paragraphs: The Leafs are still in deep offseason mode, with attention on how NHL-ready the top prospects look and what needs fixing before 2026-27. The Blue Jays are also looking ahead after a series loss to the Yankees, with more meaningful baseball still on the schedule. The Raptors are in the same quiet stretch, and the early question is whether Ja'Kobe Walter can handle more on-ball work and finish at the rim.

In Washington, Commanders camp is giving way to preseason looks, and rookie Antonio Williams is starting to force his way into the conversation. The next checkpoint is the preseason Week 2 meeting with the Lions, where the staff will sort out the studs and duds.
